question_text: A convex mirror of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ forms an image which is quarter the size of the object. The distance of the object from the mirror is
solution: For a convex mirror, $f = +20\text{ cm}$ and it forms an erect virtual image, so magnification $m = +\frac{1}{4}$. Using the mirror magnification formula, $m = \frac{f}{f - u} \implies \frac{1}{4} = \frac{20}{20 - u} \implies 20 - u = 80 \implies u = -60\text{ cm}$. Thus, the object distance from the mirror is $60\text{ cm}$.

question_text: What is the length of the optical path of two media in contact having thicknesses $2\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$ and refractive indices $1.5$ and $1.7$ respectively?
solution: The optical path length is given by $\Delta x = \mu_1 t_1 + \mu_2 t_2$. Substituting the given values: $\Delta x = (1.5)(2\text{ cm}) + (1.7)(3\text{ cm}) = 3.0\text{ cm} + 5.1\text{ cm} = 8.1\text{ cm}$.

question_text: A converging beam of light forms a point image on a screen of an object. A plane glass plate of thickness $2\text{ cm}$ and refractive index $\frac{3}{2}$ is introduced in the path of the beam. The distance by which the screen should be shifted with respect to its initial position to obtain a point image on the screen will be
solution: The normal shift produced by a glass slab of thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$ is given by $\Delta x = t\left(1 - \frac{1}{\mu}\right)$. Substituting $t = 2\text{ cm}$ and $\mu = 1.5$: $\Delta x = 2\left(1 - \frac{1}{1.5}\right) = 2\left(1 - \frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{2}{3}\text{ cm} \approx 0.67\text{ cm}$. Hence, the screen must be shifted by $0.67\text{ cm}$.

options: A plane mirror always forms a virtual image
The virtual image formed by a concave mirror is always enlarged
The critical angle is always defined in the denser medium
A parallel glass slab cannot deviate the light
solution: A plane mirror can form a real image when a converging beam of light (virtual object) is incident on it. Therefore, the statement that a plane mirror always forms a virtual image is incorrect.

options: Velocity of light is constant in all media
A convex lens always forms real image
If aperture of lens is halved then image size will be halved
The ray optics is not applicable when size of obstacle is less than wavelength of light
solution: Ray optics is valid only when the linear dimensions of obstacles or apertures are much larger than the wavelength of light ($a \gg \lambda$). When the size of the obstacle is comparable to or smaller than the wavelength, wave optics (diffraction effects) predominates, making ray optics inapplicable.

question_text: A parallel narrow beam of light travelling through water in a container is incident on an air bubble of radius $8\text{ mm}$. What will be the distance of the image obtained due to refraction of the beam at the first face of the air bubble from the centre of the bubble? $\left[\mu_{\text{water}} = \frac{4}{3}\right]$
solution: Using the spherical surface refraction formula $\frac{\mu_2}{v} - \frac{\mu_1}{u} = \frac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R}$ at the first surface: here $\mu_1 = \frac{4}{3}$, $\mu_2 = 1$, $u = -\infty$, and $R = +8\text{ mm}$. This gives $\frac{1}{v} - 0 = \frac{1 - 4/3}{+8} = -\frac{1}{24} \implies v = -24\text{ mm}$. The image is formed $24\text{ mm}$ in front of the first vertex. Since the center of the bubble is at a distance of $R = 8\text{ mm}$ behind the first vertex, the total distance of the image from the center of the bubble is $24\text{ mm} + 8\text{ mm} = 32\text{ mm}$.

question_text: Two slabs $P$ and $Q$ of transparent materials have thickness in the ratio $2 : 5$. If a ray of light takes the same time to move from $A$ to $B$ and from $B$ to $C$, then the refractive index of $Q$ with respect to $P$ will be
diagram_description: Two adjacent slabs P and Q of thicknesses in ratio 2:5 placed together. Light ray travels horizontally from A to B through slab P and then from B to C through slab Q.
solution: The time taken by light to travel through a medium of thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$ is $\Delta t = \frac{\mu t}{c}$. Since the time taken in both slabs is the same: $\mu_P t_P = \mu_Q t_Q \implies \frac{\mu_Q}{\mu_P} = \frac{t_P}{t_Q}$. Given $\frac{t_P}{t_Q} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$, the refractive index of $Q$ with respect to $P$ is $^{P}\mu_{Q} = \frac{\mu_Q}{\mu_P} = 0.4$.
